I built an open-source JANUS dossier on the UAP × nuclear question. It includes official NARA/AARO/NRC/DOE records, Los Alamos and Pantex, the 2025 Palomar nuclear-test correlation, the 2026 critique and response, French/SCU spatial datasets, our own open-data controls, and a preregistered reanalysis designed to reproduce the old signal first and then try to kill it. Current verdict: the association is interesting and unresolved; nuclear causation and nonhuman origin are not established.

There are genuine official records of unexplained or initially unidentified aerial/security events around nuclear sites, and some historical studies report statistical associations. But the strongest open-data controls also reveal major confounds: observing schedules, reporting opportunity, drone/UAS baselines, dataset definition, and sensor/plate artifacts. The nuclear-UAP association remains scientifically OPEN; nuclear causation and nonhuman origin are NOT ESTABLISHED.

The modern baseline is surprisingly important: AARO received 18 nuclear-site UAS reports in FY2024 and 50 in FY2025; FY2025 states none of those 50 were reported as UAP. This shows how much real aerial activity can occur around nuclear infrastructure without implying an anomalous craft class.

An open SCU dataset contains 590 selected UAP reports from 1945-1975 and compares atomic production, assembly, stockpile and deployment sites against civilian and non-atomic military controls. It reports elevated early-period activity, especially around 1948-1952.

A 2025 Scientific Reports paper reported that POSS-I transients were 45% more likely within +/-1 day of above-ground nuclear tests (p=0.008), and that on transient-positive days each additional UAP report was associated with an 8.5% increase in transient count.

This is not folklore: it is an official DOE-linked security record concerning an unidentified object near a nuclear-weapons facility, with ground-surveillance-radar detection, security response, visual follow-up and imagery handling in the record chain.

A formal Los Alamos-era conference considered repeated aerial/green-fireball observations around a nuclear laboratory and competing explanations. The historical fact is the institutional concern and investigation, not a solved exotic origin.
secondary_figures: A French spatial point-pattern study found population density, nuclear-risk factories/contaminated land and moisture to be significant covariates of UAP-report intensity, while residual hotspots remained unexplained by that model.

The National Archives now maintains a dedicated UAP records collection receiving material from NRC, FAA, ODNI, OSD, NSA, State, FBI, Air Force and CBP on a rolling basis. This is where future primary-source checks should start.
